title: autotune: default batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Avery Kim
description: Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost and manual tuning by providing conservative, production-safe defaults and an autotune loop that recommends batching, KV caching parameters, and quantization profiles per workload. This PR implements: 1) a new defaults system for batching/windowing and prefix KV caching tuned from production traces, 2) quantization profile discovery and a small library of validated profiles (fp16->int8/4-bit heuristics + validation harness), and 3) a unit-economics tooling surface (cli + backend) that simulates throughput/cost/latency for candidate configs and feeds recommendations back into the autotune engine. What changed (high-level): consolidated default config layer under runtime/config/defaults, added an autotune manager in runtime/autotune that scores candidate configs via a cost model, introduced quant-profiles/{profiles.json,validation_harness.py} with validated quant settings for common model families, and added a lightweight CLI (tools/uecon) and backend endpoint (/internal/uecon/simulate) to produce cost/latency estimates and suggested rollouts. Checklist: - [x] Defaults implemented and feature-flagged - [x] Quant profiles added with unit tests + validation harness - [x] Unit-econ CLI + API implemented - [x] Telemetry added for applied recommendations and rollback triggers - [x] Docs: README + quickstart for running the CLI locally - [x] E2E perf tests in perf-canary to validate latency SLOs Notes on rollout: feature-flag default_autotune=true off in prod for 48 hours; enabled in canary and staging. Autotune recommends but does not apply changes without operator approval by default. Automated rollouts can be enabled per-customer via Dedicated settings.

review_comments: Sam Patel: Overall looks great. Question: how do we avoid oscillation when autotune suggests conflicting cache sizes across different models? Can we add a sticky decay?
Avery Kim: Good point - added sticky window with exponential decay (autotune/manager.py) and tests. See commit d6b9f2a.
Diego Morales: CI failed initially on perf-canary (latency regression) - the new defaults increased tail latency on long-seq GPT models in one scenario.

Avery Kim: Investigated - regression caused by larger default batch window for seq>2048. Toned down default window when avg_seq>1024 and added per-route overrides (commit f3e4d1b). Re-ran perf-canary, tail p99 back within SLO.
Priya Shah: UX: console card should indicate confidence score (low/med/high) and a link to the simulation report. Please add a tooltip and ensure API surface returns confidence metadata.
Avery Kim: Added confidence field in API and UI tooltip; updated docs with explanation.
Sam Patel: Can we include an opt-out for automated quantization per customer? Security/compliance may require explicit review.
Avery Kim: Added customer-scoped opt-out flag and made autotune recommendations explicit by default. Documented under Dedicated->Security.
Diego Morales (LGTM): approved after tests passed and perf re-checks

release_notes:
- Add autotune defaults for batching and KV caching to reduce operator tuning burden
- Introduce curated quantization profiles (int8/4-bit) with validation harness
- Add unit-economics tooling (CLI + internal API) to simulate cost/latency tradeoffs and generate rollout recommendations
- Feature-flagged rollout; autotune recommends by default and requires explicit approval to apply changes
notes: Security: quantization profiles validated for numerical parity on a suite of regression prompts. Ops: recommended to enable in canary and monitor autotune.telemetry.autosuggest.* metrics for 72 hours before wider rollout.
